messages:
Nia (AM): opening Aurora POC thread. Customer wants Redwood Private in their AWS account, single stable outbound IP for firewall allowlist, and short security attestation. POC: 2 weeks.
Cal (SE): need clarity: do they require original client IP visible to their downstream? Also want recommendation between interface endpoints vs peering.
Omar (NetOps): short: interface endpoints (PrivateLink) give stable DNS and avoid routing table churn; peering ok only if no overlapping CIDRs. For stable egress IPs recommend NAT Gateway(s) with EIPs per AZ or NLBs with EIPs if preserving client IP via proxy-protocol.
Ruth (InfoSec): questionnaire blockers: rotating egress IPs and explicit firewall ports. We should provide one-line attestation: "No public inbound ports needed; outbound HTTPS (443) to verified FQDNs only; TLS 1.2+ enforced; customer-managed KMS supported."
Cal (SE): sample firewall rules to paste:
- Allow outbound TCP/443 to: *.redwood-inference.com
- Allow outbound TCP/443 to model artifact store (s3.amazonaws.com)
If they insist on IPs, have them allocate NAT EIPs and share the list.
Omar (NetOps): quick test for interface endpoint:
```
curl -v https://vpce-0a9b8c7d.vpce-svc-yyy.us-west-2.vpce.amazonaws.com/health -H 'Host: api.rw-inference.internal'
```
Nia (AM): pricing Q: will NAT/EIPs materially add to POC cost?
Cal (SE): yes, NAT Gateway + EIP costs apply by hour and GB; offer two POC options: reuse existing egress (low cost, SNAT) or provision dedicated NAT/EIPs (higher infra cost). We'll include a ballpark in the quote.
infra-bot: POC sandbox ready in us-west-2 (build-2045). :rocket:
Nia (AM): action items: Omar -> short diagram + curl test (today). Ruth -> attestation paragraph + cert links (tomorrow). Cal -> KMS/legal blurb (tomorrow).
